The test image shows a corn leaf with yellow-green streaking/chlorotic patterns along the veins, creating a mosaic-like appearance. This is a **leaf** symptom, narrowing to 19 candidates.

The streaking pattern points to viral/bacterial streak diseases. Top candidates: Maize_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Stewart_S_Disease, Maize_Streak_Virus, Maize_Chlorotic_Dwarf_Virus, Goss_S_Wilt.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the top candidates.
MDMV reference shows light green streaks on young leaves. Somewhat similar but the test image has broader chlorotic areas. Let me check Stewart's Disease.
Stewart's Disease shows bleached/tan necrotic streaks, quite different from the test image's yellow-green mosaic. Let me check Maize Streak Virus.
MSV shows very distinct fine streaks, much more pronounced than the test image. Let me check Maize Chlorotic Dwarf Virus.
MCDV reference shows yellow-green chlorotic patches and streaks, quite similar to the test image. Strong candidate. Let me check Goss's Wilt next.
Goss's Wilt shows large necrotic brown lesions with freckles, not matching. Let me check Corn Stunt Spiroplasma.
Not a match. Let me check Northern Leaf Blight, then revisit MCDV and MDMV for comparison.
NLB shows cigar-shaped lesions, not matching. With 2 views left, let me compare MCDV and MDMV more closely.

This second MCDV reference is an excellent match to the test image - same broad yellow-green chlorotic streaking pattern along the leaf, same diffuse vein banding appearance, same soil background context. Very strong visual similarity.

Both MCDV references show the characteristic vein banding with broad, diffuse yellow-green chlorosis running along the leaf, which closely matches the test image. MDMV by contrast shows narrower, more defined streaks. The test image's broad chlorotic pattern with vein banding is diagnostic of MCDV.
